answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants.. What makes it robust is that honest graders are financially motivated to reject the cluster, so fake votes lose their value before verdicts are tallied. Consider a meadow as the anchor of the cost.
